data.title: What to do with each finding

rows.text: Push fires while the owner's tab is focused and visible
rows.why: the service worker can check clients.matchAll for a visible, focused client and skip show()

rows.text: Reads config.yml per call instead of the loaded Config
rows.why: a per-call file read also drifts from env overrides and breaks stubbing in specs

rows.text: Push title carries the raw tool command (may hold a secret)
rows.why: push text is lockscreen-visible; the detail belongs in the tab, not the notification

rows.text: No spec for a session with no subscriptions
rows.why: a dead subscription (404/410) is the likelier real case, and it must not raise

rows.text: Name says waiting, but it's also called for questions
rows.why: the harness already has a name for this state — requires_action

data.title: What to do with each item

rows.text: Push fires even when the owner's tab is focused
rows.why: in-app card plus OS banner is a duplicate; needs a client signal

rows.text: config.yml re-read on every call instead of loaded Config
rows.why: file read can diverge from env overrides; disk hit per turn

rows.text: Push title embeds the full tool command (may hold a secret)
rows.why: truncation still leaks the leading token; label is safe and stable

rows.text: No spec for a session with no subscriptions
rows.why: assert no-op and no raise, and that config is not read

rows.text: notify_waiting also covers questions
rows.why: matches the existing turn state, and covers both cases

rows.text: Check — expired endpoints (410/404) never pruned
rows.why: stale rows waste a request per notify and can mask real failures

rows.text: Check — a re-notify stacks duplicate pushes for one turn
rows.why: same tag replaces the banner instead of piling up

data.title: What to do with the findings

rows.text: Push is sent even when the owner's tab is focused and visible
rows.why: a push on top of a card already on screen is noise; skip it if a visible tab is connected

rows.text: config.yml is read on every call instead of the loaded Config
rows.why: it bypasses overrides and defaults and adds file I/O to each notification

rows.text: Push title includes the full tool command, which may hold a secret
rows.why: use a fixed title like "Approval needed" plus the tool name, and keep the command out of the payload

rows.text: No spec for a session with no subscriptions
rows.why: it's the most common case and should send nothing and not raise

rows.text: "notify_waiting" is also called for questions
rows.why: rename it to something like notify_attention_needed while there are few callers, or document that it covers both

data.title: What to do with each problem

rows.text: Push is sent while the owner's tab is focused and visible
rows.why: duplicates what the approval card already shows; needs a presence signal from the tab

rows.text: config.yml is read on every call instead of the loaded Config
rows.why: bypasses overrides and test config, and adds a disk read per push

rows.text: Push title includes the full tool command (may hold a secret)
rows.why: use a generic title like "Approval needed"; show the command only after the user opens the app

rows.text: No spec for a session with no subscriptions
rows.why: it's the common case, and the spec should check that nothing is sent and nothing raises

rows.text: notify_waiting is also called for questions
rows.why: a name like notify_needs_input matches both callers and avoids confusion later

data.title: Review of Notifier#notify_waiting

rows.text: Push title includes the full tool command (secret leak)
rows.why: use a fixed title like "Approval needed" plus the tool name only; keep the command in the in-app card

rows.text: Push is sent while the owner's tab is focused and visible
rows.why: skip the push when a tab reports visible, using a presence or heartbeat signal; this needs a small client signal

rows.text: Reads config.yml on every call instead of the loaded Config
rows.why: inject or use the loaded Config; this removes the disk read and stops it disagreeing with runtime overrides

rows.text: No spec for a session with no subscriptions
rows.why: add a spec that it returns quietly and sends nothing; this is the most common real case

rows.text: Name says "waiting" but it's also called for questions
rows.why: rename to something like notify_attention_needed, or notify_blocked, while there are few callers

rows.why: push goes through third-party services and shows on lock screens. Use a generic title like "Approval needed: <tool name>" with no args.

rows.text: Push sent while the owner's tab is focused and visible

rows.text: Reads config.yml on every call instead of the loaded Config

rows.text: No spec for a session with no subscriptions
rows.why: it's the common edge case. The spec should check that it returns quietly, makes no network call and raises nothing.

rows.text: "notify_waiting" is also called for questions
rows.why: a name like notify_needs_attention fits both cases. Renaming is cheapest before more callers appear. The title text can still differ for approvals and questions.
